nodes.reconstructed_theorem:
Let E be any finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space, including the zero-dimensional case, equipped with its Borel measurable structure and canonical volume. Let V:E->R be C^2. Let alpha,beta be nonnegative real parameters satisfying 0<alpha<=beta. At every x in E and for every v in E assume
  alpha ||v||^2 <= D^2 V(x)[v,v] <= beta ||v||^2.
Let eta>0 satisfy beta eta<=1.

Define mu as the normalized exponential tilt of volume by -V. Define J as the pushforward of mu times the standard Gaussian on E under (x,z) |-> (x,x+sqrt(eta) z), and let nu be its second marginal. For each y in E define S(y) to be the normalized exponential tilt of volume in variable x by
  -V((y+x)/2) - ||y-x||^2/(8 eta).
These are the specified actual-input measures, rather than supplied kernel or compatibility assumptions.

Then nu is a probability measure. There exists a real partially defined linear map G from scalar L^2(nu) to E-valued L^2(nu), whose domain is dense in the entire scalar L^2(nu), which is closable and whose closure is closed. For every scalar L^2 class a and vector L^2 class b, (a,b) belongs to the graph of G if and only if there is a single C^infinity compactly supported real function phi on E such that a=phi and b=grad phi nu-almost everywhere. Here grad phi is the Euclidean gradient represented in E. Closability means the topological closure of this graph is still the graph of a single-valued partial linear map; that map is denoted by closure(G).

For this G there exist one bounded real linear operator T: L^2(nu)->L^2(nu) and one bounded real linear operator K: L^2(nu)->L^2(nu;E) such that, simultaneously for every arbitrary scalar L^2(nu) class u,
  (Tu,Ku) belongs to the graph of closure(G),
  ||Tu||_2 <= ||u||_2,
  Tu(y) = integral u(x) dS(y)(x) for nu-almost every y,
  u and the function x |-> u(x)^2 are both integrable against S(y) for nu-almost every y,
  eta ||Ku||_2^2 <= [(1-alpha eta)^2/(4(1+alpha eta))] (||u||_2^2-||Tu||_2^2),
  4 eta ||Ku||_2^2 <= ||u||_2^2-||Tu||_2^2.
All L^2 norms and all almost-everywhere equalities in this conclusion use nu. Integrals against S(y) use the chosen strongly measurable representative of the L^2 class u. Each almost-everywhere assertion is for the given u, so the theorem does not assert a single exceptional null set valid for every u.

Thus Tu has gradient Ku in precisely the closed compact-gradient sense defined by G. The assertion does not identify this closure with a separately specified weak-Sobolev space or give pointwise C^1 regularity of Tu. It imposes no centering, smoothness, compact support, extra moments, or derivative hypotheses on the arbitrary input u. The endpoint alpha eta=1 is allowed, as is rank zero. No algorithmic iteration, convergence, mixing, query cost, or main-paper result is asserted; no optimality proof for the displayed sharp coefficient is included in the statement.
